newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says needs $15.7 bln in aid in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says needs $15.7 bln in aid in 1997.

text.p: Indonesia said on Tuesday it needs $15.7 billion in foreign aid to finance a total of 648 government-proposed projects this year.

"We released a blue book containing 648 government-proposed projects. The value of the projects are $19.91 billion, and $15.7 billion is needed in foreign project assisstance," National Development Planning Agency deputy chairman Rahadi Ramelan told reporters.
"Although we need $15.7 billion in aid, we know we won't get the full amount because donor countries will not pledge that much," Ramelan said.
He said Indonesia will continue to seek loans from countries that did not attach political conditions. He did not elaborate.
The projects would be put forward at the Consultative Group for Indonesia (CGI) meeting in Tokyo, possibly in June.
The World Bank-chaired CGI consists of 20 countries, including Japan, and several other financing agencies.
The CGI pledged $5.26 billion in aid to Indonesia in 1996, compared with $5.35 billion in 1995.
Ramelan said projects in the transportation, education, mines and energy and social sectors will get top priority.
"Infrastructure and human resource development projects are still our priority," he said.
He said Indonesia, one of the biggest debtor countries with outstanding foreign loans totalling some $100 billion, proposed 689 projects worth $21.24 billion in 1996.
